text: Seabrook Town mostrou raça para virar a partida contra Harbour City, vencendo por 4 a 2 após um emocionante segundo tempo. Apesar do primeiro tempo equilibrado e dos gols de Elias Okafor e Marek Barros para Harbour City, com um estilo de passes curtos e pacientes[#905][#975], o time visitante mudou a estratégia aos 65 minutos para um estilo mais direto e pressão alta, que funcionou muito bem. Essa mudança levou Seabrook a marcar 3 gols na segunda etapa, incluindo dois gols decisivos de Kian Romano nos acréscimos, com chances bem claras, ou seja, com altas probabilidades de gol[#1361][#1882][#1906]. No total, Seabrook chutou 22 vezes, com 9 finalizações certas e um xG (chances reais de gol) de 3.53, muito mais do que Harbour City, que fez 10 chutes e teve um xG de 1.26. Marek Barros brilhou no time da casa, com 1 gol, 2 assistências e nota 10, mesmo com a derrota[#975].

Marek Barros foi o destaque da partida, mas não evitou a derrota do Harbour City contra Seabrook Town.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in pt

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals, overcoming Harbour City's 2 goals for a final 4-2 win [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Kian Romano scored twice in injury time (90+2' and 90+3') with high xG values of 0.554 and 0.994, securing the late comeback [#1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) had the highest player rating of 10.0 with 1 goal, 2 assists, 4 tackles, and 5 key passes despite his team losing [#975].
- Harbour City had 10 shots with 5 on target and an xG of 1.26, while Seabrook Town had 22 shots, 9 on target and an xG of 3.53, showing Seabrook's more dominant attacking stats [team_stats].
- Seabrook Town increased pressing and directness after 65' in a tactical change which preceded their comeback with 3 second-half goals [#1361, goals at 69', 90+2', 90+3'].

- Seabrook Town’s comeback was driven by a tactical shift at 65', where their coach Mara Lindholm instructed a higher press, more direct play, and raised defensive line height to chase the game. This led to increased pressure (press 0.84 vs 0.66), more direct passing (0.57 vs 0.42), and a higher line (0.72 vs 0.6), which improved their attacking threat and helped them score 4 goals in the second half [#1361].
- The initial Harbour City goal at 45' was a patient build-up with 17 passes over 57 seconds reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and ‘patient short passing’ style. Marek Barros’s through assist and Elias Okafor finishing showed their patient, structured approach to breaking down the defense [#904,905].
- Seabrook Town’s goals after the tactical change often came from regains and rapid transitions, demonstrating an effective counter-press and quick direct play consistent with the coach's instructions and their typical wide crossing style. For example, the goal at 69' was built from a regain with quick passes and a through ball assist leading to Callum Varga’s finish [#1447,1448].
- Kian Romano’s late goals (90+2' and 90+3') illustrate Seabrook’s ability to exploit counter-attacks and quick interplay in tight situations, reflective of their more direct attacking style post-tactical change and use of wide play and crossing to create close-range chances [#1881,1882,1905,1906].
- Harbour City’s style under Tomasz Rhee relied on controlled possession and patient passing but they had lower pressing intensity and a deeper defensive line as indicated by their higher PPDA (7.9 overall) and fewer field tilt stats. Their late tactical change to increase pressing and directness was too late to stem Seabrook’s momentum [#1361,#1884].
- The formations reinforced these patterns: Harbour City’s 4-2-3-1 favored possession and build-up through the midfield (evidenced by many passes and involvement of attacking midfielders like Barros), while Seabrook Town’s 3-4-3 allowed wide attacking options and wing overloads for crossing and fast direct plays leading to their four goals [team_styles].
